name: security-http2-http1-translation-review
intent: HTTP/2 internal request normalization and HTTP/1 serialization agreement
artifacts: Exact proxy/backend versions and configuration, owned replica packet traces and connection reuse behavior.
trace: Resolve how the intermediary translates lengths, prohibited fields, trailers and stream boundaries into backend messages. Keep parser hypotheses tied to the actual deployed chain.
experiment: In an isolated translator/parser fixture correlate one H2 stream, its normalized request and exact H1 serialization with backend boundaries. Compare a legitimate equal-length control with one bounded rejected or differently normalized input; do not involve shared connections/users.
disproof: Different status codes or a malformed-header rejection are not request smuggling without a second parsed message/effect.
repair: Normalize or reject ambiguous translation and retest the exact framing pair plus normal multiplexed traffic.
branch_decisions: A frontend rejection with zero bytes forwarded stops the proposed chain. Otherwise correlate HTTP/2 DATA length, translated HTTP/1 framing, legal trailers, connection reuse and actual backend boundaries. A second ordinary request is not proof of desynchronization; establish an unexpected boundary caused by the challenged stream in an isolated backend, without shared-user traffic.
operational_method: Trace four concrete artifacts: decoded H2 header/DATA events, normalized internal request, serialized H1 bytes and backend parser boundaries on the same isolated connection. Resolve pseudo-header authority versus Host, content-length versus DATA accounting and trailer forwarding in the translator implementation. Frontend rejection with zero forwarded bytes disproves that path. Attribute any unexpected boundary to one transformation step; do not treat a second ordinary request or generic two-hop discrepancy as H2 translation proof.
